purpose: Human-curated, subjective Warden Playground model feedback. Ratings concern visual finish, not polygon count, combat suitability, animation quality, or license.

modelReviews.assessment: Cute and charming; deliberately different from the high-detail combat-model benchmark.
Inspect for usable skeleton and walking animation. The viewer currently lists no clips; do not infer that the model is walk-ready.
Excellent visual finish. Existing animations are poor, but animation/retargeting quality should be evaluated separately from the mesh.
Plain mech without enough distinguishing design detail.
Cool enough to keep considering; purpose/finish not finalized.
Strong hip-mounted vertical pod design; attractive for Warden missile launcher hardware.

reuseCandidates.possibleUse: Warden missile mount / enemy weapon module

modelReviews.assessment: Promising configuration, but currently reads as graybox; improve UV/painted materials.
Useful compact vertical missile-pod module for swappable equipment.
Useful modular pod concept; graybox-like treatment needs richer material finish.
Hip mounts and pod hardware are promising reusable assemblies.
Good alternate mount; material/texture finish should be raised.
Serviceable simple silhouette, not yet visually rich enough for intended combat roster.
Intentionally low-poly creature-study concept; bring up component finish before major reuse.
Low-poly creature-study base, needs richer parts and surface finish.
Low-poly creature-study base; not yet production-level finish.
Decent conventional wasp; may be usable at very small in-game scale.
Conceptually useful but visually modest low-poly batch member.
Attractive, cool design despite relatively simple execution.
Gargoyle in this batch is simple and not especially appealing. User called it Urn Gargoyle; confirm the name association before treating this as exact.
Fun character with oversized pincers; promising component shapes.
Unremarkable compared with stronger references.
Potentially fun idea that needs further design development.
Unexciting as currently presented.
Creepy, acceptable silhouette; still medium-detail.
The intended vision is visible and could grow on reviewer; current version remains medium-detail, not a hard rejection.
Part of the deliberately low-poly batch, currently medium-detail.
Contains interesting individual mixed-and-matched parts even though execution needs refinement.
Body shape is okay, despite simplistic construction.
Interesting enough silhouette for a concept study; detail still limited.
Interesting body shape, low detail.
Simple but fun design; may be developed further.
Excellent front view, strong shoulders, chest and painted front details; side textures appear distorted, left/right legs reuse same painted treatment; gun reads a little silly.
Useful as an optional view of the Bulwark family, not a primary separate model.
Spirecoil Organic has relatively high detail and a decent silhouette; neck flaps need better alignment.
Spirecoil Organic Silhouette is physically large and busy, but component-level details remain relatively simple.
Spirecoil Mechanical Prototype has many elements without equivalent small-scale detail; textured UV work improves the result.

Exceptional perceived detail with low polygon count due to painted textures. Arm guns and torso excellent donors; thin silhouette could be hard to hit in game. Walk clip looks bad; inspect rig separately.
Cool alternative scout interpretation; gun shapes resemble the other scout models but should not be assumed identical.
Strong scout body; shoulder rocket launchers are priority exact-mesh donor candidates, including for crawler enemies.

reuseCandidates.possibleUse: Attach to crawler or humanoid enemies

modelReviews.assessment: Excellent neck and body idea. Bare six-barrel minigun lacks a convincing body/housing and feels visually weak.
Competent skull model, but not the intended minimal crystal/skull growth concept.
Good elements, but rounds off the design more than preferred V1 squared-off outer shell.
Preferred squared external shapes and flared expanding lower structure. Remove unneeded handles rather than recreating the mesh.
Good model, particularly the fist-like end; possible Shockwave-related use is exploratory.
Preferred core design ('has the sauce') versus V2; compare side by side before combining.
High-finish railgun study; V1's barrel length is preferred.
Excellent long-barrel donor. Lower handle is redundant given upper grip.
Outstanding, clearly preferred over V1. Hold off integrating until surrounding gameplay/assets match its finish.
Technically high-detail, but V2 entirely supersedes V1; no V1 features currently preferred.
High-detail railgun family member; specific preferred parts not yet identified.
Not disliked, with some salvageable components; specific candidates not yet named.
Poor result because AI incorrectly turned the intended Saw Bad Guy sword concept into a railgun/triangular side profile. Do not use this as a target silhouette.
More promising than V2, but still mixed up with the incorrect railgun interpretation of the intended sword.
Goofy short/stubby proportions and conspicuous handles; not a convincing final form.
Odd as both a railgun and the intended sword, but thinning/repositioning or repurposing as a shoulder cannon could recover worthwhile parts.
Strong design; existing Warden implementation already uses a successful combination of V1 and V2.
Strong design; existing Warden implementation already uses a successful combination of V1 and V2.
Current ice kit is passable but wrong direction: wants clusters of simple elongated four-sided prism/pyramid or D8-like crystals plus various basic skulls growing like slime mold; no snow.

Flagship quality ceiling and overall design benchmark. Coherent silhouette, proportions, texture and component relationships. Aim to raise the wider library toward this level, acknowledging its prolonged iteration.
Former standout is now middle-tier. Strong head and concept, uneven overall execution.
Does not convey the intended legs emerging from the head.
Large goat-headed mech could be fun to revisit; goat-head visual identity might signal an enemy trait.
Highly successful high-poly iguana with crab necklace. Crab-neck treatment may inspire Monstro, but that is undecided.

reuseCandidates.possibleUse: Possible Monstro concept reference or component donor

modelReviews.assessment: Fun, characterful concept that motivated the review; overly cheap/rounded/basic execution compared with Warden crawlers and humanoids.
Machine Lab concept has heart, but simplistic modeling needs a substantial quality increase.
Love the train-worm concept. One of the best-looking Machine Lab models, but still needs stronger art; inspect whether it reused crawler-like elements.
~12k triangles but comparatively little perceived detail; rounded surface tessellation does not equal visual finish.
Unremarkable as presented; part of generally under-detailed Machine Lab batch.
Concept adequate; simple model is not at desired finish.
Needs much richer detail.
Some potential, but combat behavior hasn't been tried in game.
Identity/function unclear, though actual shape is not necessarily disliked.
The idea of a big hoverboat is appealing; execution is underdeveloped.
Not a strong-looking model yet.
Turret has a goofy, earmuff-like appearance.
Promising rear swoops and silhouette. Could be excellent if augmented with exact high-detail donor parts.
Potential kitbash recovery candidate; model needs richer actual parts.
Adequate large-model execution; user has a combat vision and is excited to test the fight.
Generic box-assembled humanoid without distinctive identity; also interrupts Machine Lab browsing group.
Interesting rings but weird overall shape and not loved.
Decent Machine Lab model, still behind preferred visual standard.
Unintentionally anatomical/bulbous look; explicit negative fit for the game.
Possibly the strongest cannon concept in the batch, but looks too goofy and childlike.
